home.heroIntroduction: I'm Brian. I build intuitive interfaces, reliable APIs, and data-intensive platforms, from the first prototype to production at scale.
home.about: Most recently, I worked as a Senior Software Engineer at Mobian, building search, analytics, reporting, data-processing, and reliability features for an audience-intelligence and advertising platform. Before that, I built clinical-study tools at Faro Health and led frontend modernization work for Cams at Various Inc.
home.section1Content1: In my most recent role as a Senior Software Engineer at pharmaceutical tech startup Faro Health, I built and optimized REST and CQRS-based microservices and UI modules using TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Jest, and React. I developed feature slices and POCs, designed and executed technical solutions, wrote unit and integration tests, optimized application performance, and built deployment pipelines with GitHub Actions.
home.section1Content2: Previously, I led an international remote front-end team at Various Inc., collaborating closely with designers to modernize legacy JavaScript and Perl-based video streaming apps. We migrated them to a scalable, high-performance React and TypeScript stack with Next.js, MOBX, WebSockets, and Python, backed by REST APIs and a CI/CD pipeline for seamless deployment.

experience.title: Experienced
experience.summary: I build and improve production software across product interfaces, APIs, data systems, search, and cloud infrastructure. My recent work at Mobian connected those layers across audience-intelligence and advertising workflows.
experience.scope: Earlier roles included clinical-study tools at Faro Health and frontend modernization for Cams at Various Inc. The timeline highlights how that work has evolved across products, teams, and technical boundaries.
experience.copy1: Most recently, I worked as a Senior Software Engineer at Mobian, building search, analytics, reporting, data-processing, and reliability features for an audience-intelligence and advertising platform.
experience.copy2: I built and refined search, filtering, pagination, autocomplete, CSV exports, statistics, cache behavior, ingestion tooling, and reporting workflows across Next.js, React, TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Snowflake, Dagster, Redis, and AWS.
experience.copy3: The work regularly crossed frontend, backend, ETL, search, and infrastructure boundaries. I also handled production fixes, test coverage, release coordination, brand reconciliation, and integrations across the frontend, Persona API, Content API, Video Brand Safety, ETL, and end-to-end testing repositories.
experience.copy4: Before Mobian, I helped build Faro Health's clinical-study design platform, contributing frontend features, service integrations, testing, and delivery improvements.
experience.copy5: Earlier at Various Inc., I led frontend modernization work for Cams, moving high-traffic real-time video and chat experiences toward a more scalable React, TypeScript, Next.js, WebSocket, and Python platform.

leadership.title: Technical Leader
leadership.copy1: I've led and collaborated with distributed teams across the US, Europe, Taiwan, and China, working across product, design, engineering, data, and infrastructure.
leadership.copy2: My approach is practical: establish clear technical direction, reduce unnecessary complexity, surface risks early, and keep teams focused on shipping reliable work. At Mobian, that often meant coordinating changes across several services and repositories while preserving data contracts, search behavior, release stability, and the user experience.
leadership.copy3: I'm comfortable moving between architecture and implementation, designing systems, debugging production issues, reviewing tradeoffs, improving development workflows, and helping teams turn broad requirements into concrete, maintainable solutions.

1.summary: Product features, service integrations, testing, and delivery improvements for a clinical-study design platform.

overview.title: Clinical-study design platform
overview.content: I contributed to Faro Study Designer, a healthcare product used to plan, document, and evaluate clinical protocols. My work focused on shipping maintainable product features across TypeScript, React, service integrations, PostgreSQL-backed workflows, automated tests, and deployment pipelines.

features.label: Product features
features.detail: Built frontend and backend feature slices for study-design workflows

integrations.label: Service integration
integrations.detail: Integrated UI modules with REST and CQRS-style service boundaries

testing.label: Reliability
testing.detail: Improved reliability with unit and integration tests

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.detail: Supported delivery through GitHub Actions and repeatable release practices

outcome.content: The result was clearer product behavior, stronger test coverage, and a more maintainable path for evolving clinical-study features.

2.summary: Frontend modernization for live discovery, video, chat, and interactive session workflows.

overview.title: Cams real-time product modernization
overview.content: I led frontend modernization work for Cams, a mature high-traffic platform with live discovery, video, chat, public rooms, and private interactive sessions. The work required preserving active product behavior while moving legacy JavaScript and Perl-backed experiences toward a scalable React, TypeScript, Next.js, WebSocket, and Python architecture.

leadership.label: Team leadership
leadership.detail: Coordinated an international frontend team across product, design, and engineering priorities

discovery.label: Product workflows
discovery.detail: Improved discovery, presence, chat, and session-state interfaces

realtime.label: Real-time behavior
realtime.detail: Supported real-time UI updates without disrupting long-running media experiences

modernization.label: Modernization
modernization.detail: Moved product surfaces into a more maintainable frontend stack

outcome.content: The outcome was a clearer and more dependable foundation for real-time interaction-heavy workflows on an established production platform.

3.summary: A civic website helping residents understand proposed planning changes and participate in the process.

overview.title: San Anselmo city planning website
overview.content: A WordPress website for the 2025 San Anselmo General Plan Update that provides residents with information on proposed changes to the town's infrastructure, zoning, and public spaces. It includes project updates, sustainability initiatives, transportation improvements, and public surveys for community feedback.

4.summary: A maintainable marketing site for a San Francisco Bay Area design and development agency.

overview.title: Launch Brigade website
overview.content: Launch Brigade is a web design and development agency based in the San Francisco Bay Area. I contributed to a responsive digital presence focused on clear content structure, maintainable presentation, and communicating the agency's work.

5.summary: A proof of concept that transformed study-design data into flexible reporting views.

overview.title: Data analytics dashboard proof of concept
overview.content: The Data Analytics Dashboard was a Pandas-based proof of concept that used Study Designer data stored in a star schema to create an analytics microservice and frontend. It allowed users to explore study data across the dimensions most relevant to their work.

6.summary: Identity-provider-agnostic SSO for organizations using their own authentication services.

overview.title: Faro B2C SSO implementation
overview.content: An identity-provider-agnostic single sign-on implementation for Study Designer. It allowed organizations to use their own SAML and OAuth identity providers to issue tokens for interacting with the application API.

7.summary: A product website explaining how data and machine learning support dealership inventory decisions.

overview.title: LotLinx website
overview.content: LotLinx is an AI-driven automotive inventory management platform that uses machine learning and data analytics to help dealerships optimize inventory turnover and profitability. The site communicates real-time insights into market demand, pricing strategies, and consumer behavior.

8.summary: Frontend prototype work for a cloud platform focused on intricate additive-manufacturing models.

overview.title: Metafold 3D MVP
overview.content: Metafold 3D is a cloud platform for designing and engineering complex models optimized for additive manufacturing. I contributed frontend prototype work for visualizing and working with intricate geometries such as lightweight lattice structures.

9.summary: A connected search experience spanning interactive interfaces, APIs, indexes, caches, and exports.

challenge.title: Complex audience data needed to feel immediate
challenge.content: Advertisers needed to discover, analyze, and act on dense audience and channel data without understanding the systems behind it. Search behavior had to remain consistent across filtering, pagination, historical reporting, and exports.

architecture.title: One search contract across the stack

exports.label: Redis + streaming exports
exports.detail: Fast reads and filter-aware CSV output

discover.label: Discover
discover.title: Define the audience workflow
discover.content: I translated advertiser discovery needs into consistent requirements for search, filtering, pagination, historical reporting, and exports.

connect.label: Connect
connect.title: Join APIs, indexes, and data stores
connect.content: I coordinated FastAPI services, PostgreSQL queries, OpenSearch indexes, and Redis caching behind a shared search contract.

interact.label: Interact
interact.title: Make discovery feel immediate
interact.content: I built server-side autocomplete, infinite scrolling, date filtering, channel statistics, and responsive result states in React and Next.js.

export.label: Export
export.title: Carry user context into exports
export.content: Streaming CSV exports preserved the active search and filter parameters instead of becoming a disconnected workflow.

validate.label: Validate
validate.title: Test the full experience
validate.content: I verified behavior across the interface, API boundaries, search infrastructure, and data services so each path produced consistent results.

outcome.content: The result connected discovery, analysis, and export into one coherent experience, with the same active search context preserved from the interface through backend processing.

10.summary: A recovery-aware ingestion system for normalizing, classifying, and diagnosing contextual data at production scale.

challenge.title: Messy URLs become expensive at scale
challenge.content: Duplicate URLs, incomplete metadata, asynchronous jobs, and inconsistent classifications compound quickly. The work focused on making every stage observable and recoverable rather than treating ingestion as a single request.

ingest.label: Ingest
ingest.title: Receive contextual inputs
ingest.content: I developed tooling that accepted webpage, video, and channel inputs across asynchronous processing paths.

normalize.label: Normalize
normalize.title: Create stable URL identities
normalize.content: URL parsing, normalization, aliases, and fallbacks turned inconsistent inputs into comparable records.

dedupe.label: Dedupe
dedupe.title: Reconcile repeated work
dedupe.content: Deduplication and alias reconciliation reduced redundant processing while preserving the correct canonical relationships.

classify.label: Classify
classify.title: Apply consistent context
classify.content: Batch processing and downstream integrations carried normalized metadata into classification workflows.

persist.label: Persist
persist.title: Save durable metadata
persist.content: I improved metadata persistence and checkpoints so completed work could be reused across services.

recover.label: Recover
recover.title: Make failures diagnosable
recover.content: Retry behavior, checkpoints, and CloudWatch diagnostics made serverless failures easier to resume and investigate.

outcome.content: The tooling made high-volume processing easier to resume, diagnose, and reconcile across multiple Python services, serverless functions, storage systems, and downstream consumers.

11.summary: Entity reconciliation and reporting workflows that made different ad platforms behave like one product.

challenge.title: Different platforms described the same business differently
challenge.content: FreeWheel and Google Ad Manager used different identifiers, reporting structures, and naming conventions. Users still needed one predictable way to find advertisers, distinguish duplicates, map placements, and retrieve reporting data.

pipelines.label: Data pipelines
pipelines.detail: Snowflake, Dagster, PostgreSQL, and reporting caches

workflows.label: Product workflows
workflows.detail: Search, galleries, mappings, and CSV exports

connect.label: Connect
connect.title: Integrate external ad systems
connect.content: I built advertiser and reporting-entity search across FreeWheel and Google Ad Manager data.

reconcile.label: Reconcile
reconcile.title: Resolve entity differences
reconcile.content: Source-qualified selections and duplicate-name disambiguation preserved identity across platforms.

sync.label: Sync
sync.title: Coordinate reporting data
sync.content: I improved reporting caches and the transformations connecting Snowflake, Dagster, and PostgreSQL workflows.

present.label: Present
present.title: Build predictable product workflows
present.content: Search, galleries, mappings, and exports gave users one consistent surface over fragmented sources.

outcome.content: The resulting tools made advertising entities easier to navigate and targeting information easier to select while keeping source identity and reporting relationships explicit.

12.kicker: Making a multi-service platform more reliable
12.summary: Cross-repository infrastructure, testing, observability, and release work for a production advertising platform.

frontend.label: Frontend
frontend.detail: Authenticated Cypress and initial Playwright coverage

infrastructure.label: AWS infrastructure
infrastructure.detail: Scheduled Lambda jobs, ingestion, and CloudWatch diagnostics

identify.label: Identify
identify.title: Trace issues across services
identify.content: I investigated failures across frontend, APIs, ETL, Persona, and AWS infrastructure rather than treating symptoms in isolation.

improve.label: Improve
improve.title: Strengthen tests and infrastructure
improve.content: Authenticated Cypress coverage, initial Playwright tests, scheduled Lambda jobs, and configuration fixes reduced release risk.

release.label: Release
release.title: Coordinate cross-repository delivery
release.content: I aligned dependent changes and framework security updates across repositories and service boundaries.

monitor.label: Monitor
monitor.title: Close the production feedback loop
monitor.content: CloudWatch diagnostics and release follow-through made operational behavior visible after deployment.

outcome.content: The work connected test coverage, serverless processing, framework security, service configuration, ETL synchronization, and coordinated releases across frontend and backend systems.

13.kicker: Building consistent interfaces across a complex product
13.summary: Reusable components and semantic design foundations that connected complex backend behavior to clear product interactions.

challenge.title: A growing analytics product needed a shared interface language
challenge.content: Dashboards, tables, galleries, and search tools were evolving alongside new datasets and workflows. The interface needed reusable patterns that could absorb that complexity without making every feature feel different.

tokens.label: Semantic tokens
tokens.detail: Shared visual language and Material UI variants

patterns.label: Interaction patterns
patterns.detail: Autocomplete, filters, pagination, and loading states

integration.label: Data integration
integration.detail: Frontend API behavior translated into clear state

audit.label: Audit
audit.title: Find repeated UX problems
audit.content: I identified inconsistencies across dashboards, tables, galleries, search, filters, and loading states.

systemize.label: Systemize
systemize.title: Build reusable interface patterns
systemize.content: Semantic tokens, Material UI variants, and shared React components replaced one-off decisions.

integrate.label: Integrate
integrate.title: Connect patterns to real data
integrate.content: The components translated complex API behavior, pagination, autocomplete, and exports into clear state.

validate.label: Validate
validate.title: Protect the product workflows
validate.content: Jest, Cypress, and Playwright coverage verified authenticated paths and reduced regressions.

outcome.content: Reusable React components and shared patterns reduced one-off interface decisions while making complex search, export, and reporting workflows easier to understand and test.
